nodes.label: docs/canon/README.md — the entry point to the committed record: what the user actually said, the contradiction map, and the pile of documents that talk about them. Interpretation, produced 2026-08-03, unreviewed by the user; an agent wrote this file and the documents beside it in a few hours, and all are listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md. Read it before anything else in docs/canon/.

docs/canon/ was established 2026-08-03 to settle one question: what did the user actually say. Agent inventions had been accumulating as rules — an agent wrote a term or a number, a later agent recorded it as "the user's", a third enforced it as a hard rule. The standing instruction, given the day before: "i fucking demand you filter through every fucking memory and chatlog you have and find out everything I HAVE SAID, THOROUGHLY" and "Search the entire repo for exactly ALL information I (the user, fucking ME) i have conveyed, the actual things I ACTUALLY SAID: all conversations, memories, logs, docs, data, diffs, committs, changes, fixes and code.. that means you have to search the entire git-repo also with all the fucking branches etc" — both 2026-08-02.

Two files carry the work. raw/user_turns_all.md is the evidence — his 1,304 turns, the only source of intent, cited by line. CONTRADICTION_MAP.md is the live list of where those rulings and the system disagree, each collision layered, cited, and carrying what fixing it takes: an engine change, a graph rebuild, a doc correction, or a ruling only he can give. Everything else in the folder is reference, opened when a specific claim is in dispute.

The record has an end date and it is not today. Check raw/user_turns_all.jsonl's last timestamp before citing the corpus as the record: it is a snapshot, not a live feed, holding what had been said when the extractor last ran, and every ruling given after that exists in conversation only until someone writes it down. Keeping it current is two steps, both at commit time, and CLAUDE.md's hard rules require them: the ruling lands in the file that owns it — CONTRADICTION_MAP.md for a collision, OPEN_DECISIONS.md for something still open, the code or v3/CONSTANTS.md for a constant or a flag — before the reply goes out; and the corpus is extended so it carries the turn itself, because a ruling recorded only in an interpretation document is an agent's paraphrase with no source behind it, which is the condition the 08-02 mining order was given to end.

Extend by union, never overwrite. tools/canon_extract.py reads Claude Code transcripts and Claude Code deletes old ones, so the corpus is not reproducible from its sources: a re-run on 2026-08-05 gained 106 turns and lost one, 2026-07-06 08:07 ("ok, exactly where are we with the whole artefact concept/build?"), whose session file is gone from disk, and the committed corpus is now its only copy. Union a fresh extraction into the committed one, account for every turn the run drops, and only then write. A plain re-run silently destroys evidence, and the arithmetic in raw/EXTRACT_REPORT*.md describes the pass that produced the file — it does not describe what a later pass would produce.

Three kinds of thing, and none of them is authority. Intent — what was supposed to be built — has one source, the user's own typed turns (raw/user_turns_all.jsonl / .md), and its one honest caveat is that a machine decided what counted as a human turn: across both machines 11,137 user-role records were seen and 10,244 were rejected by a named rule, leaving 803 turns, and the corpus has since been extended by union to 1,304 turns through 2026-08-13 18:10, with the two files agreeing again — same rows, same count, the .md rendered from the .jsonl. Two of those 1,304 exist only because the .md carried them: turns whose session transcript Claude Code has since deleted, kept through the union and marked in the rendering as recovered from this record. State — what actually exists — is the git history plus the code, the graph and the run outputs: re-run the command and you get the same answer, it is nobody's opinion, and it proves something was built but never that it was intended or correct. Interpretation — claims about intent or state — is every document in the project, this file included, all unreviewed, each holding only as far as its citations, and nothing in that tier outranks anything else in it: CANON_AUDIT.md adjudicates other documents, and that does not lift it out of the pile.

The asymmetry, and it is the whole point: state is evidence of drift from intent, never justification for it. "It is in the code" and "the commit says so" are not arguments — they are the thing being questioned, and something built against the record is a finding, not a defence. REVIEW_REGISTER.md lists the whole pile, one row per artifact, every row unreviewed: a state doc, a memory entry, CLAUDE.md, an agent definition, this file — interpretation, none of it intent.

A statement being written in this repo is not evidence he said it. Only a [CHAT] quote is, and a [CHAT] quote is checkable in the corpus. "you do understand that just because the text is in the repo, that doesnt mean i was the one that ok'd it or put it there, right? you literally put shit in writing and pretend its canon" and "ok, you do realise \"verified by me\" means YOU verified? and not me?" — both 08-02.

The file table and each file's standing. raw/user_turns_all.jsonl / .md — the corpus, both machines merged, chronological, no edits: 1,304 verbatim turns to 2026-08-13, both files in agreement; intent, the only source of it, machine-filtered. raw/user_turns.* and raw/user_turns_desktop.* — the two halves before merge, laptop 793 (from 07-06), desktop 127 (from 05-14). raw/EXTRACT_REPORT*.md and raw/rejected_sample*.md — the filter's own accounting, one pair per machine; tool output, read to judge how much intent the filter dropped. CONTRADICTION_MAP.md — every statement of his that something contradicts, layered (V1-GRAPH / V1-ENGINE / V1-ORIGINAL / V2-DESIGN / V3-NATIVE / CROSS): 12 live collisions with the remedy each needs, 12 tensions awaiting his judgement, 14 near-collisions scoping dissolves, and the standing uncontradicted record. USER_CANON.md — 469 quotes arranged into 13 design subjects, 10 working-relationship subjects, a 60-row timeline and a never-built inventory, with the choosing, grouping and headings agent judgement and 115 entries second-hand [DOC] recoveries. CANON_AUDIT.md — 117 prescriptive repo claims adjudicated: 65 GROUNDED, 17 AGENT-ORIGIN, 11 CONTRADICTS-USER, 24 STALE; verdicts are not rulings. OPEN_DECISIONS.md — unruled reversals, what was specified and never built, unanswered questions, the 17 instructions no agent surface carries, audit findings awaiting a ruling. DESIGN_HISTORY.md — git record plus desktop design docs merged into one chronological design history. The review apparatus, raw/git_record.md (74 commits, 91 reproduce commands, 18 numbered contradictions), raw/desktop_docs_record.md (20 agent-written docs, ~150 recovered quotes, 80 labelled rulings), and the two machines' memory copies frozen at 2026-08-03.

The corpus arithmetic, per machine and merged, produced by tools/canon_extract.py and reproducible from the files in raw/; the two machines were extracted in separate passes and then concatenated, so each machine has its own accounting and the merged totals are the sums. User-role records seen: laptop 10,313 · desktop 824 · merged 11,137. Rejected by a named rule (machine-authored, not typed by the human): 9,547 · 697 · 10,244. Duplicates collapsed (same turn replayed into a branch/resume copy of a session): 90 · 0 · 90. Kept as human-authored — the corpus: 676 · 127 · 803. Collapsed at merge time: 0. The identity holds exactly in every column — seen = kept + rejected + collapsed — by construction, not by luck: the extractor counts one seen per user record and then sends that record down exactly one of three exits, and there is no fourth outcome.

What each corpus number is not, since every published miscount so far has come from mixing them up. 10,313 and 9,547 are laptop-only and not merged totals, so quoting them as the caveat on the 803-turn corpus silently drops the desktop's 824 seen and 697 rejected. 10,313 − 9,547 = 766 is not a corpus size and never was: it omits the 90 collapsed duplicates, and 766 − 90 = 676 is the laptop half, which the desktop's 127 brings to 803 — a bare subtraction of seen minus rejected is wrong wherever duplicates were collapsed. "Merged and deduped" was wrong: the merge removed nothing (0 collapses, and the two halves share no uuid, no (timestamp, text) pair and no session), so 676 + 127 = 803 with no removal is exactly right. The 90 are branch/resume artifacts, not repeated messages — all 90 matched on (timestamp, text) to the millisecond across sibling copies of one session and 0 matched on uuid, while genuinely repeated text survives (14 distinct texts appear more than once, 54 rows in total). The false-negative audits are per-machine and used different methods: laptop audited the 6,380 harness_template rejects three ways with 0 human turns lost; desktop has no harness_template reject at all, its 620 tool_result rejects provably carry zero characters of human text, and all 77 remaining rejects were read individually.

Coverage and where it stops. 1,304 turns, 2026-05-14 → 2026-08-13 — laptop 1,177 + desktop 127, as both raw/user_turns_all.md and its .jsonl twin stand after the 2026-08-13 union; nothing has ever been removed at merge time and the two halves do not overlap, while the split halves (user_turns.* 793, user_turns_desktop.* 127) are the 2026-08-03 snapshot and no longer sum to the merged corpus — 384 laptop turns have been unioned in since, and the desktop half cannot be re-extracted from this machine at all. Nothing before 05-14 survives as chat: the first commit is 2026-05-07, and that first week — the 52-file Neo4j pipeline, the 12-entry decision log, the original graph schema, the controlled canonical vocabulary — survives only as state, in the git history, with what was intended that week unrecoverable. Two chat blackouts, 05-16 → 05-26 (11 days) and 05-29 → 06-26 (29 days), zero human turns on either machine, holding the v2 pivot, the facet redesign, the closing of the graph spine, the death of the chunk description, the build gate, the eval-harness design and the RAGAS-only purge — and no chat is not no record, since 20 dated design docs and git cover both windows as interpretation and state, never intent.

Thin days are thin, not silent: six of the 33 active days carry one to three turns — 05-27 (1), 05-28 (1), 07-01 (3), 07-02 (2), 07-12 (3), 07-27 (2). Absence of a statement on a date proves nothing. An earlier agent called 2026-07-15 "the first day" of the project — the earliest date in one partial local extract, wrong by two months. Do not repeat it.

How to re-derive all of it, from the repo root using the miniconda python: python tools/canon_extract.py for the laptop half; the same with --machine desktop --name user_turns_desktop --no-sweep --sources pointed at the OneDrive _desktop_transcripts folders for the desktop half; --merge laptop=… desktop=… --name user_turns_all to merge; and --verify 15 --verify-floor 5 to spot-check kept turns byte-for-byte against their source transcripts. The per-machine seen and rejected figures are not recoverable from raw/*.jsonl, which hold only what was kept — they come from the extraction reports, whose per-rule tables sum to the rejected totals (laptop 6,380 + 2,530 + 373 + 202 + 45 + 16 + 1 = 9,547; desktop 620 + 29 + 21 + 17 + 10 = 697) — and a fresh run will report a larger seen than 10,313 because the laptop transcripts are live and still growing.

raw/ is evidence, and read-only — the corpus, the two hand-built records (git_record.md, desktop_docs_record.md) and the memory copies alike. The corpus is re-derived with the tool, never edited. The records and the copies are frozen at their date: they are what was believed then, and a claim inside one that the corpus contradicts is settled in CONTRADICTION_MAP.md by citing the turn that contradicts it — never by rewriting the record, which erases the evidence the map rests on. The documents in this folder are the layer that gets corrected.

When you disagree with him: the record is what he said, not what an agent concluded he meant. About to state what he wants? Find the quote first, and if there is no quote say there is no quote. Where two of his quotes conflict, both stand — listed in OPEN_DECISIONS.md §1 — so do not pick a winner, do not reconcile them in a doc, and do not build to one and record the other as superseded. A conflict between the record and what you believe is correct is raised as a question in the conversation, in plain English, never resolved silently in code or in a doc. Never "correct" his current intent with an older note: what he names, he wants, and that is the spec. And do not open v3/data/questions.jsonl, gold100.jsonl, heldout100.jsonl or 10smoke.jsonl while doing design work — 08-02: "honestly, you should not have the questions/gold available to you, there is 0% good that can come out of taht".
